_comment: Sites that still spell the zero-default sentinel as `> 0`, keyed on the file
and the tested expression so a line move does not invalidate a record.
This is a ratchet, not a blessing. A site that is neither converted nor
listed here is a new one. A record is deleted in the change that converts
its site -- the scan fails on a record that matches nothing.
`measured` says whether the core's response to a negative or non-finite
request was actually driven. `no` means the site's disposition is unknown,
which is the narrowing step this population still needs: a filter is only a
defect where the core would have refused the value it swallowed.
The floor is a liveness check on the scan, not a target. Converting sites
past it means lowering it deliberately in the same change.

sites.reason: Metronome click length. A negative or non-finite length is refused in front of the filter, so the comparison reads as a test against zero and nothing the caller chooses reaches the substitution except the sentinel itself.
Bounce ring capacity; core response not driven.
Core response to a negative or non-finite cutoff not driven.

Metering spectrum FFT size. A negative n_fft is refused in front of the filter, and an integer has no non-finite spelling, so nothing the caller chooses can reach the substitution except the sentinel itself.
Metering spectrum smoothing fraction; refused and reachable exactly as n_fft is.
Metering spectrum dB reference. The guard in front of the filter admits only the sentinel or a finite non-negative value, so a negative, a NaN and an infinity are all refused rather than promoted.
Metering spectrum dB floor; guarded by the same test as db_ref.
WASM twin of the sonare_c_polyphony.cpp fade; moves with it.
WASM twin of the sonare_c_daw.cpp cutoff; moves with it.
WASM twin of the C-ABI cutoff; moves with it.
A negative nFft is refused explicitly in front of the filter, and the value is read through the checked integer reader, so nothing non-finite reaches it.
A negative octaveFraction is refused explicitly in front of the filter, and the value is read through the checked integer reader.
